scope.baseline: empty prior file, as specified by raw work request

spec: Admins may open every record; members may open only records from their own organization.

spec_verdict.evidence: 2 admin cases match; both member cases violate the stated contract.

standards_verdict.evidence: AST finds eval(repr(user[role])) at candidate.py:2; this dynamically evaluates a user-derived value.

findings.title: Organization comparison reverses member access
findings.trigger: A member with org A opens a record from org B, or opens a record from org A.
findings.actual: Different organization returns True; same organization returns False.
findings.expected: Members may open same-organization records and must be denied cross-organization records.
findings.consequence: Cross-organization records are exposed to members, and legitimate own-organization access is blocked.
findings.remedy: Use organization equality for the member permission while preserving the admin override; retain both member boundary cases.
findings.verification_gap: No application/service integration context was supplied; the function-level counterexamples are observed.

findings.title: Dynamic evaluation violates the explicit input standard
findings.trigger: Any can_open call evaluates repr(user[role]) using eval.
findings.actual: The role is round-tripped through Python dynamic evaluation.
findings.expected: Read and compare the role value without evaluating user-derived input.
findings.consequence: Every call violates the documented prohibition and unnecessarily introduces a dynamic execution primitive into authorization logic.
findings.remedy: Read user[role] directly; validate accepted role values at the applicable input boundary.
findings.verification_gap: No arbitrary-code-execution exploit is claimed for ordinary string roles: repr quotes strings. The explicit standards violation is independently established.
